column6: Ihre Weltanschauung hat sich nach der Reise verändert.
column7: Her worldview changed after the trip.
column8: Weltanschauung entered English, French, and Italian untranslated in the 19th century, a testament to the German Romantic tradition of systematic thought.

column6: Nachhaltigkeit ist ein zentrales Thema in der deutschen Politik.
column7: Sustainability is a central topic in German politics.
column8: The word predates modern environmentalism by centuries: it was coined by a Saxon forester in 1713 for sustainable timber management.

column5: due to / on the basis of
column6: Aufgrund der Krise wurde das Projekt verschoben.
column7: Due to the crisis, the project was postponed.
column8: 'Aufgrund' takes the genitive and is preferred over 'wegen' in formal writing: the distinction marks register more sharply than in other languages.

column6: Er schaute mit stiller Schadenfreude zu.
column7: He watched with quiet Schadenfreude.
column8: One of the world's best-known German loanwords, it entered English dictionaries in the 1920s. Philosophers from Nietzsche to Russell have written about it at length.

column6: Das Paket wird morgen geliefert.
column7: The package will be delivered tomorrow.
column8: 'Werden' serves as the passive auxiliary: the future tense, the passive voice, and 'to become' are all governed by the same verb.

column6: Im Winter liebe ich die Gemütlichkeit zu Hause.
column7: In winter I love the cosiness at home.
column8: From 'gemütlich': a warm, intimate, relaxed atmosphere, hard to translate with a single word.

column6: Ich möchte eine Beschwerde über die Lieferung einreichen.
column7: I would like to file a complaint about the delivery.
column8: You say 'eine Beschwerde einreichen' (to file) or 'Beschwerde einlegen'. It comes from 'sich beschweren' (to complain).

column5: the desire to travel and explore
column6: Ihre Wanderlust treibt sie jedes Jahr in ein neues Land.
column7: Her Wanderlust drives her to a new country every year.
column8: It entered English in the 19th century during Romanticism, reflecting the Romantic elevation of nature, travel, and self-discovery to philosophical ideals.

column6: In Deutschland ist die Krankenversicherung Pflicht.
column7: In Germany, health insurance is mandatory.
column8: Germany invented mandatory health insurance in 1883 under Bismarck: the world's first national system, still a model for many countries.

column5: to presuppose / to take for granted
column6: Diese Stelle setzt fließende Deutschkenntnisse voraus.
column7: This position presupposes fluent German.
column8: 'Vorausgesetzt, dass...' ('provided that...') introduces a condition typical of German contractual language.

column6: Diese Aussage ergibt nur im richtigen Zusammenhang Sinn.
column7: This statement only makes sense in the right context.
column8: 'Im Zusammenhang mit' ('in connection with') is an omnipresent connective in German academic and journalistic prose.

column6: Ich war von ihrer Rede tief beeindruckt.
column7: I was deeply impressed by her speech.
column8: It comes from the past participle of 'beeindrucken': many German adjectives ending in '-t' are actually participles.

column6: Angesichts der Lage müssen wir schnell handeln.
column7: Given the situation, we have to act quickly.
column8: It takes the genitive and belongs to a high register: you find it in editorials, not in chat messages.

column6: Man sollte seine Vorurteile hinterfragen.
column7: One should question one's own prejudices.
column8: Literally 'judgment before': the compound 'Vor- + Urteil' makes visible that prejudice is a verdict passed too early.

column6: Wir müssen alle Faktoren berücksichtigen.
column7: We have to take all factors into account.
column8: A long, formal verb typical of minutes and reports: in speech people would more likely say 'daran denken' (to think of that).

column6: Einerseits ist es teuer, andererseits spart man Zeit.
column7: On the one hand it's expensive, on the other you save time.
column8: The pair 'einerseits ... andererseits' is the preferred structure for balanced German argument: it's taught in school as an essay pattern.

column6: Die Auseinandersetzung mit der eigenen Geschichte ist wichtig.
column7: Engaging critically with one's own history is important.
column8: The word oscillates between 'quarrel' and 'in-depth critical engagement': in German intellectual discourse it almost always means the latter.

column6: Das Projekt wird voraussichtlich im Herbst abgeschlossen.
column7: The project is expected to be completed in autumn.
column8: Omnipresent in Deutsche Bahn announcements: 'voraussichtliche Ankunft' is the estimated arrival, not a promise.

column6: Er verzichtete zugunsten seiner Kollegin auf die Beförderung.
column7: He gave up the promotion in favor of his colleague.
column8: It takes the genitive. Its opposite, 'zulasten' ('at the expense of'), is frequent in economic and legal language.

column6: Ich kann deine Entscheidung gut nachvollziehen.
column7: I can well relate to your decision.
column8: Different from 'verstehen': 'nachvollziehen' means mentally retracing someone else's reasoning until it makes sense.

column6: Bezüglich Ihrer Anfrage melde ich mich nächste Woche.
column7: Regarding your request, I'll get back to you next week.
column8: It takes the genitive and is the standard opening phrase of formal German emails, often abbreviated 'bzgl.'.

column6: Die Pressefreiheit ist eine wichtige demokratische Errungenschaft.
column7: Freedom of the press is an important democratic achievement.
column8: It's not a personal success but a collective, lasting one: used for rights, institutions, and social progress.

column6: Die Gesellschaft verändert sich ständig.
column7: Society is constantly changing.
column8: 'Gesellschaft' means both 'society' in the civic sense and 'company' commercially, as in 'Aktiengesellschaft' (stock corporation).

column6: Die Öffentlichkeit reagierte schockiert.
column7: The public reacted with shock.
column8: 'Öffentlichkeit' comes from 'öffentlich' (public) with the abstract suffix '-keit', denoting the collective body of citizens.

column6: Weltoffenheit prägt viele Großstädte.
column7: Open-mindedness shapes many big cities.
column8: 'Prägen' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to shape, deeply characterize'.

column6: Das ist eine gesamtgesellschaftliche Aufgabe.
column7: This is a society-wide task.
column8: A long compound typical of the sociological and political register, combining 'gesamt' (whole) and 'gesellschaftlich' (societal).

column6: Die Globalisierung hat viele Vorteile und Risiken.
column7: Globalization has many advantages and risks.
column8: 'Globalisierung' entered German in the 1990s, a conceptual loan now fully naturalized.

column6: Die Digitalisierung verändert die Arbeitswelt.
column7: Digitalization is changing the world of work.
column8: Germany is often criticized internally for being relatively slow with the Digitalisierung of public administration.

column6: Automatisierung ersetzt manche Berufe.
column7: Automation is replacing some jobs.
column8: 'Ersetzen' takes a direct accusative object and is often used in discourse about the future of work.

column6: Der Strukturwandel trifft ganze Regionen.
column7: Structural change is hitting entire regions.
column8: German coal regions like Lausitz have been undergoing a deep economic Strukturwandel for decades.

column6: Soziale Ungleichheit nimmt zu.
column7: Social inequality is increasing.
column8: 'Zunehmen' is separable and means 'to increase', very common in discourse about social and economic trends.

column6: Bildung soll Chancengleichheit schaffen.
column7: Education should create equal opportunity.
column8: 'Chancengleichheit' combines the French loanword 'Chance' with 'Gleichheit' (equality), a hybrid typical of political language.

column6: Diskriminierung ist gesetzlich verboten.
column7: Discrimination is legally prohibited.
column8: Germany's equal-treatment law ('Allgemeines Gleichbehandlungsgesetz') explicitly bans every form of discrimination.

column6: Persönlicher Kontakt kann Vorurteile abbauen.
column7: Personal contact can break down prejudices.
column8: 'Abbauen' takes the accusative and is separable, used for both prejudices and physical structures.

column6: Viele Deutsche haben einen Migrationshintergrund.
column7: Many Germans have a migration background.
column8: The official German term 'Migrationshintergrund' is statistically defined and used in national demographic studies.

column6: Meinungsfreiheit ist ein Grundrecht.
column7: Freedom of speech is a fundamental right.
column8: Freedom of opinion is enshrined in Article 5 of the German constitution, the Grundgesetz.

column6: Zensur widerspricht demokratischen Werten.
column7: Censorship contradicts democratic values.
column8: 'Widersprechen' takes the dative: 'demokratischen Werten', a verb with the always-inseparable prefix 'wider-'.

column6: Desinformation verbreitet sich schnell online.
column7: Disinformation spreads quickly online.
column8: 'Sich verbreiten' is reflexive and means 'to spread', very common in discourse about social media.

column6: Man sollte Fake News kritisch hinterfragen.
column7: One should critically question fake news.
column8: 'Hinterfragen' isn't separable and means 'to critically question, examine'.

column6: Journalisten müssen ihre Quellen prüfen.
column7: Journalists must check their sources.
column8: 'Quelle' means both 'information source' and 'water spring' — the same metaphor of an origin.

column6: Objektivität ist im Journalismus wichtig.
column7: Objectivity is important in journalism.
column8: 'Objektivität' is nearly identical across languages, a shared philosophical term of Latin origin.

column6: Voreingenommenheit erschwert eine faire Debatte.
column7: Bias makes a fair debate harder.
column8: 'Erschweren' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to make difficult', a formal verb common in academic register.

column6: Manipulation durch Medien ist ein reales Risiko.
column7: Manipulation through the media is a real risk.
column8: 'Durch' always takes the accusative, used to indicate the tool or medium through which an action happens.

column6: Verantwortungsbewusstsein sollte man früh lernen.
column7: A sense of responsibility should be learned early.
column8: A very long compound typical of German: 'Verantwortung' + 'Bewusstsein', a productive pattern in the formal register.

column6: Bürgerbeteiligung stärkt die lokale Demokratie.
column7: Civic participation strengthens local democracy.
column8: Many German cities have official 'Bürgerbeteiligung' forums for local urban-planning decisions.

column6: Über dieses Thema gab es eine Volksabstimmung.
column7: There was a referendum on this topic.
column8: Unlike Switzerland, referendums at the federal level are extremely rare in Germany by constitutional law.

column6: Die Koalition einigte sich auf einen Kompromiss.
column7: The coalition agreed on a compromise.
column8: Coalition governments are the norm in German politics, given the proportional electoral system.

column6: Beide Seiten mussten einen Kompromiss schließen.
column7: Both sides had to reach a compromise.
column8: 'Einen Kompromiss schließen' is the standard fixed collocation, like 'einen Vertrag schließen' (to sign a contract).

column6: Die Verhandlungen dauern schon Wochen.
column7: The negotiations have been going on for weeks.
column8: 'Verhandlung' also means 'court hearing' in a legal context, besides general 'negotiation'.

column6: Bei diesem Fall besteht ein Interessenkonflikt.
column7: There's a conflict of interest in this case.
column8: 'Bestehen' often takes no preposition or 'aus', and is irregular: 'besteht, bestand, bestanden'.

column6: Lobbyarbeit beeinflusst manche Gesetze.
column7: Lobbying influences some laws.
column8: 'Lobbyarbeit' combines the English loanword 'Lobby' with the German word 'Arbeit' (work), a common hybrid compound.

column6: Bürger fordern mehr Transparenz von der Regierung.
column7: Citizens are demanding more transparency from the government.
column8: 'Fordern von' takes the dative: 'von der Regierung' — the standard structure for a demand directed at an entity.

column6: Korruption schadet dem Vertrauen in Institutionen.
column7: Corruption harms trust in institutions.
column8: 'Schaden' takes the dative: 'dem Vertrauen', one of the most common dative verbs in German.

column6: Machtmissbrauch untergräbt die Demokratie.
column7: Abuse of power undermines democracy.
column8: 'Machtmissbrauch' = 'Macht' (power) + 'Missbrauch' (abuse). The prefix 'miss-' marks a wrong use: 'missbrauchen', 'Missverständnis'.

column6: Die Gewaltenteilung schützt vor Machtmissbrauch.
column7: Separation of powers protects against abuse of power.
column8: 'Gewaltenteilung' combines 'Gewalt' (power) and 'Teilung' (division), a fundamental German constitutional concept.

column6: Der Rechtsstaat garantiert gleiche Rechte für alle.
column7: The rule of law guarantees equal rights for all.
column8: 'Rechtsstaat' combines 'Recht' (law) and 'Staat' (state): a central principle of the postwar German constitutional system.

column6: Das Grundgesetz trat 1949 in Kraft.
column7: The Basic Law took effect in 1949.
column8: The 'Grundgesetz' is formally Germany's constitution, named this way to underline its supposedly temporary character after the country's division.

column6: Das Verfassungsgericht prüft die Gesetzmäßigkeit.
column7: The constitutional court reviews lawfulness.
column8: Germany's Federal Constitutional Court, in Karlsruhe, enjoys enormous moral and institutional authority in the country.

column6: Föderalismus prägt das deutsche System.
column7: Federalism shapes the German system.
column8: German federalism distributes broad powers to the sixteen Bundesländer, especially over education and culture.

column6: Der Tag der Deutschen Einheit ist ein Feiertag.
column7: German Unity Day is a public holiday.
column8: October 3rd, the day of the 1990 reunification, is Germany's official national holiday.

column6: Der Mauerfall veränderte Europa.
column7: The fall of the Wall changed Europe.
column8: The Mauerfall of November 9, 1989, is one of the most significant events in recent German and European history.

column6: Die Wiedervereinigung brachte große Herausforderungen.
column7: Reunification brought great challenges.
column8: 'Bringen' is irregular in the Perfekt: 'brachte, gebracht', with the vowel changing twice.

column6: Ein Zeitzeuge erzählte von der DDR.
column7: A contemporary witness talked about the GDR.
column8: 'Zeitzeuge' combines 'Zeit' (time) and 'Zeuge' (witness): someone who personally lived through a historic event.

column6: Deutschland pflegt eine intensive Erinnerungskultur.
column7: Germany cultivates an intense culture of remembrance.
column8: 'Erinnerungskultur' describes the structured, institutionalized way Germany confronts its own historical past.

column6: Das Mahnmal erinnert an die Opfer.
column7: The memorial commemorates the victims.
column8: 'Erinnern an' always takes the accusative: 'an die Opfer' — a common fixed structure in memorial contexts.

column6: Die Forschung macht große Fortschritte.
column7: Research is making great progress.
column8: Germany invests heavily in scientific research, especially at institutes like the Max Planck Society.

column6: Wissenschaftler warnen vor den Folgen.
column7: Scientists are warning about the consequences.
column8: 'Warnen vor' takes the dative: 'vor den Folgen' — a common fixed structure for expressing a warning.

column6: Die Hypothese muss noch getestet werden.
column7: The hypothesis still needs to be tested.
column8: 'Getestet werden' is passive: 'werden' plus a participle, the standard structure in scientific language.

column6: Die Forscher führen ein Experiment durch.
column7: The researchers are conducting an experiment.
column8: 'Durchführen' is separable: 'führen durch' in the present tense, with the long prefix detached at the end.

column6: Die Ergebnisse werden sorgfältig ausgewertet.
column7: The results are being carefully evaluated.
column8: 'Auswerten' is separable and takes the accusative, a technical verb typical of data analysis.

column6: Laut Statistik sinkt die Geburtenrate.
column7: According to statistics, the birth rate is falling.
column8: 'Laut' takes the genitive or the dative and is the standard phrase for citing statistical sources.

column6: Datenanalyse ist heute in fast jedem Beruf gefragt.
column7: Data analysis is in demand in almost every profession today.
column8: 'Gefragt sein' means 'to be in demand', often used for professional skills.

column6: Der Algorithmus entscheidet, was wir sehen.
column7: The algorithm decides what we see.
column8: 'Algorithmus' comes from the name of the Persian mathematician al-Khwarizmi, via medieval Latin.

column6: Diese Erkenntnis war überraschend.
column7: This finding was surprising.
column8: 'Erkenntnis' comes from 'erkennen' (to recognize, understand), a key term in epistemology (Erkenntnistheorie).

column6: Diese Theorie wird viel diskutiert.
column7: This theory is much debated.
column8: 'Wird diskutiert' is the present passive: 'werden' plus a participle, the standard structure in academic register.

column6: Es gibt keinen eindeutigen Beweis.
column7: There's no clear proof.
column8: 'Kein eindeutiger Beweis' uses 'kein' to negate the noun directly, a structure typical of German.

column6: Die neue Studie widerlegt die alte Theorie.
column7: The new study disproves the old theory.
column8: 'Widerlegen' isn't separable: it belongs to the group of verbs with the always-inseparable prefix 'wider-'.

column6: Die Ergebnisse bestätigen unsere Annahme.
column7: The results confirm our assumption.
column8: 'Bestätigen' isn't separable: it belongs to the group of verbs with the always-inseparable prefix 'be-'.

column6: Wissenschaft und Glaube schließen sich nicht aus.
column7: Science and faith don't exclude one another.
column8: 'Sich ausschließen' is mutually reflexive and means 'to exclude one another', a special reflexive use.

column6: Philosophie stellt grundlegende Fragen.
column7: Philosophy asks fundamental questions.
column8: 'Grundlegend' comes from 'Grund' (foundation) and 'legen' (to lay): literally 'that which lays the foundation'.

column6: Ethik spielt in der Medizin eine große Rolle.
column7: Ethics plays a big role in medicine.
column8: 'Eine Rolle spielen' ('to play a role') is an idiom that matches English almost exactly.

column6: Moral verändert sich im Laufe der Zeit.
column7: Morality changes over the course of time.
column8: 'Im Laufe der Zeit' ('over the course of time') takes the genitive, a common fixed expression in historical discourse.

column6: Wer trägt die Verantwortung für diesen Fehler?
column7: Who bears responsibility for this mistake?
column8: 'Tragen' means both 'to carry physically' and, abstractly, 'to bear/take on'.

column6: Das ist ein echtes moralisches Dilemma.
column7: That's a real moral dilemma.
column8: 'Dilemma' is nearly identical across languages, a shared Greek loanword.

column6: Dieser Fall ist ein echter Grenzfall.
column7: This case is a real borderline case.
column8: 'Grenzfall' combines 'Grenze' (border) and 'Fall' (case): a case sitting at the edge of a category.

column6: Aus dieser Perspektive sieht alles anders aus.
column7: From this perspective everything looks different.
column8: 'Aussehen' is separable: 'sieht aus' in the present tense, used to describe how something appears.

column6: Reisen verändert oft das Weltbild.
column7: Travel often changes one's worldview.
column8: 'Weltbild' combines 'Welt' (world) and 'Bild' (image): a compound nearly identical to 'Weltanschauung' but more colloquial.

column6: Das Bewusstsein für Umweltprobleme wächst.
column7: Awareness of environmental problems is growing.
column8: 'Bewusstsein für' takes the accusative: 'für Umweltprobleme' — a common structure in social discourse.

column6: Unsere Wahrnehmung ist subjektiv.
column7: Our perception is subjective.
column8: 'Wahrnehmung' comes from 'wahrnehmen' (to perceive), a separable verb with the unusual prefix 'wahr' (true).

column6: Diese Interpretation überzeugt mich nicht.
column7: This interpretation doesn't convince me.
column8: 'Überzeugen' takes a direct accusative object with no preposition, a verb common in critical discourse.

column6: Die Symbolik des Films ist komplex.
column7: The film's symbolism is complex.
column8: 'Symbolik' describes the systematic use of symbols in a work of art, literature, or cinema.

column6: Der Dichter verwendet eine starke Metapher.
column7: The poet uses a strong metaphor.
column8: 'Verwenden' takes a direct accusative object with no preposition, a verb common in literary analysis.

column6: Die Romantik war eine wichtige Epoche.
column7: Romanticism was an important era.
column8: 'Epoche' is nearly identical across languages, a shared literary-historical term of Greek origin.

column6: Diese künstlerische Strömung entstand im 20. Jahrhundert.
column7: This artistic movement arose in the 20th century.
column8: 'Strömung' means both 'water current' and 'cultural movement' — the same flow metaphor.

column6: Die Avantgarde brach mit alten Traditionen.
column7: The avant-garde broke with old traditions.
column8: 'Brechen mit' takes the dative: 'mit alten Traditionen' — a fixed structure for expressing a clean break.

column6: Zeitgenössische Kunst polarisiert oft.
column7: Contemporary art is often polarizing.
column8: 'Zeitgenössisch' comes from 'Zeitgenosse' (contemporary person), literally 'companion of one's own time'.

column6: Die Ästhetik des Gebäudes gefällt nicht jedem.
column7: Not everyone likes the building's aesthetics.
column8: 'Gefallen' takes the dative: 'nicht jedem gefallen', a structure inverted compared to English 'to like'.

column6: Kritiker üben scharfe Kritik am Konzept.
column7: Critics are voicing sharp criticism of the concept.
column8: 'Kritik üben an' takes the dative: 'am Konzept' (contraction of 'an dem') — a formal fixed structure.

column6: Die Rezension war sehr positiv.
column7: The review was very positive.
column8: 'Rezension' is more formal and specific than 'Kritik' when referring to a published critical piece.

column6: Das Publikum applaudierte lange.
column7: The audience applauded for a long time.
column8: 'Publikum' is always a singular collective noun, like 'Team' or 'Personal', even referring to thousands of people.

column6: Die Inszenierung war modern und mutig.
column7: The staging was modern and bold.
column8: 'Inszenierung' comes from 'in Szene setzen' (to stage), a technical term in theatre and film.

column6: Die Uraufführung war ein großer Erfolg.
column7: The premiere was a great success.
column8: 'Uraufführung' combines the prefix 'Ur-' (original, first) with 'Aufführung' (performance).

column6: Die Handlung des Romans ist komplex.
column7: The novel's plot is complex.
column8: 'Handlung' means both 'narrative plot' and, more generally, 'action, deed'.

column6: Der Wendepunkt der Handlung überraschte alle.
column7: The plot twist surprised everyone.
column8: In German creative writing, a well-built 'Wendepunkt' is considered essential for maintaining narrative tension.

column6: Die literarische Figur entwickelt sich stark.
column7: The literary character develops a great deal.
column8: 'Figur' describes a literary or film character, different from 'Charakter', which is a real person's personality.

column6: Das deutsche Bildungssystem ist föderal organisiert.
column7: The German education system is organized federally.
column8: Every German Bundesland has its own authority over education, creating sixteen slightly different school systems.

column6: Sie besucht das Gymnasium.
column7: She attends the Gymnasium.
column8: The Gymnasium is the school track that prepares directly for university, distinct from the Realschule and Hauptschule.

column6: Nach der Realschule macht er eine Ausbildung.
column7: After the Realschule he does an apprenticeship.
column8: The Realschule offers a middle path between the academic Gymnasium and the more practical Hauptschule.

column6: Sie hat letztes Jahr das Abitur gemacht.
column7: She finished her Abitur last year.
column8: The Abitur is the German equivalent of the school-leaving exam, required for direct university entry.

column6: Medizin hat einen strengen Numerus clausus.
column7: Medicine has a strict Numerus clausus.
column8: In some German faculties, especially medicine, the Numerus clausus requires an almost perfect school average.

column6: Der Lehrplan wird ständig aktualisiert.
column7: The curriculum is constantly being updated.
column8: 'Wird aktualisiert' is the present passive, a common structure for describing ongoing institutional processes.

column6: Sie studiert Pädagogik.
column7: She studies pedagogy.
column8: 'Pädagogik' comes from the Greek 'paidagogos' (one who guides children), the origin of 'pedagogue' across European languages.

column6: Frontalunterricht wird zunehmend kritisiert.
column7: Frontal teaching is increasingly criticized.
column8: Many contemporary German educators prefer more interactive methods over traditional Frontalunterricht.

column6: Inklusion bedeutet gemeinsames Lernen für alle.
column7: Inclusion means shared learning for everyone.
column8: 'Inklusion' describes integrating students with disabilities into mainstream classes, a central topic in German schools today.

column6: Chancengerechtigkeit bleibt eine Herausforderung.
column7: Fairness of opportunity remains a challenge.
column8: International studies repeatedly show that family background strongly affects school success in Germany.

column6: Frühförderung hilft benachteiligten Kindern.
column7: Early intervention helps disadvantaged children.
column8: 'Benachteiligt' is the past participle of 'benachteiligen' (to disadvantage), used as an adjective.

column6: Lebenslanges Lernen wird immer wichtiger.
column7: Lifelong learning is becoming ever more important.
column8: 'Lebenslang' combines 'Leben' (life) and 'lang' (long): literally 'long throughout life'.

column6: Die Firma bietet ein gutes Weiterbildungsangebot.
column7: The company offers a good range of further education.
column8: A typical long compound: 'Weiterbildung' (continuing education) + 'Angebot' (offering).

column6: Der Fachkräftemangel betrifft viele Branchen.
column7: The skilled labor shortage affects many industries.
column8: 'Betreffen' takes a direct accusative object with no preposition, a formal verb used in economic contexts.

column6: Er sucht noch einen Ausbildungsplatz.
column7: He's still looking for an apprenticeship position.
column8: The German dual system offers thousands of Ausbildungsplätze every year across dozens of different trades.

column6: Sie geht zweimal pro Woche in die Berufsschule.
column7: She goes to vocational school twice a week.
column8: In the German dual system, apprentices alternate between working at a company and classes at the Berufsschule.

column6: Ich mache im Sommer ein Praktikum.
column7: I'm doing an internship in the summer.
column8: Many German degree programs require a mandatory Praktikum before graduation, often lasting several months.

column6: Für diese Stelle brauchst du Berufserfahrung.
column7: For this position you need professional experience.
column8: 'Berufserfahrung' combines 'Beruf' (profession) and 'Erfahrung' (experience), a key term on German CVs.

column6: Die Personalabteilung meldet sich bald.
column7: HR will be in touch soon.
column8: 'Sich melden' is reflexive and means 'to get in touch', very common in workplace contexts.

column6: Sie ist eine erfahrene Führungskraft.
column7: She's an experienced manager.
column8: 'Führungskraft' combines 'Führung' (leadership) and 'Kraft' (force), a formal term for a manager.

column6: Das jährliche Mitarbeitergespräch steht bevor.
column7: The annual performance review is coming up.
column8: 'Bevorstehen' is separable and means 'to be imminent', a formal verb used for scheduled events.

column6: Die Zielvereinbarung wird jedes Jahr besprochen.
column7: The goal agreement is discussed every year.
column8: 'Besprechen' isn't separable: it belongs to the group of verbs with the always-inseparable prefix 'be-'.

column6: Die Unternehmenskultur hier ist sehr offen.
column7: The company culture here is very open.
column8: 'Unternehmenskultur' combines 'Unternehmen' (company) and 'Kultur' (culture), a key term in HR management.

column6: Die Hierarchie in diesem Unternehmen ist flach.
column7: The hierarchy in this company is flat.
column8: Many German tech companies proudly promote 'flache Hierarchien' (flat hierarchies) as a competitive advantage.

column6: Der Entscheidungsprozess dauert oft lange.
column7: The decision-making process often takes a long time.
column8: 'Entscheidungsprozess' combines 'Entscheidung' (decision) and 'Prozess' (process), typical of managerial language.

column6: Ihr Führungsstil ist eher kooperativ.
column7: Her leadership style is rather cooperative.
column8: 'Eher' means 'rather, more tending toward', used to soften a statement without being absolute.

column6: Eigeninitiative wird hier sehr geschätzt.
column7: Initiative is highly valued here.
column8: 'Geschätzt werden' is passive: 'werden' plus a participle, a common structure for describing valued workplace traits.

column6: Belastbarkeit wird in Stellenanzeigen oft verlangt.
column7: Resilience under pressure is often required in job ads.
column8: 'Verlangen' takes a direct accusative object and often appears in the requirements of German job postings.

column6: Flexible Arbeitszeiten fördern die Work-Life-Balance.
column7: Flexible hours promote work-life balance.
column8: 'Fördern' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to promote', very common in corporate language.

column6: Bei uns gilt Gleitzeit.
column7: We have flexitime here.
column8: 'Gleitzeit' combines 'gleiten' (to glide, move freely) and 'Zeit' (time): hours that 'glide' freely within certain limits.

column6: Sie plant ein Sabbatical nach zehn Jahren.
column7: She's planning a sabbatical after ten years.
column8: 'Sabbatical' is a direct loanword from English, increasingly common among mid-career German professionals.

column6: Er nimmt sechs Monate Elternzeit.
column7: He's taking six months of parental leave.
column8: In Germany, fathers also often take Elternzeit, encouraged by a benefits system designed for both parents.

column6: Gute Kinderbetreuung ist schwer zu finden.
column7: Good childcare is hard to find.
column8: 'Schwer zu finden' takes the infinitive with 'zu', the standard structure for expressing difficulty.

column6: Die Ganztagsschule wird immer beliebter.
column7: All-day school is becoming more popular.
column8: Traditionally German schools ended at midday, unlike in many other countries; the Ganztagsschule is a more recent development.

column6: Das Gesundheitswesen steht vor großen Herausforderungen.
column7: The healthcare system faces major challenges.
column8: 'Stehen vor' takes the dative: 'vor großen Herausforderungen' — a common fixed structure in institutional discourse.

column6: Es fehlen Pflegekräfte in vielen Krankenhäusern.
column7: Many hospitals lack care workers.
column8: 'Fehlen' takes the dative with an inverted subject: 'es fehlen Pflegekräfte' describes a general shortage.

column6: Altenpflege ist ein anspruchsvoller Beruf.
column7: Elderly care is a demanding profession.
column8: 'Anspruchsvoll' comes from 'Anspruch' (demand, claim): literally 'full of demands', i.e. demanding.

column6: Meine Großmutter lebt in einem Pflegeheim.
column7: My grandmother lives in a nursing home.
column8: In Germany, choosing a Pflegeheim is often guided by official quality ratings published online.

column6: Die Behandlung erfolgt ambulant.
column7: The treatment is done on an outpatient basis.
column8: 'Ambulant' contrasts with 'stationär' (inpatient): the key distinction in the German healthcare system.

column6: Er wurde stationär aufgenommen.
column7: He was admitted as an inpatient.
column8: 'Aufgenommen werden' is passive, used to describe formal hospital admission.

column6: Sie arbeitet in der Chirurgie.
column7: She works in surgery.
column8: 'Chirurgie' comes from Greek via Latin, a widely shared international medical term.

column6: Ich brauche eine Überweisung zum Facharzt.
column7: I need a referral to a specialist.
column8: In Germany you often need a 'Überweisung' from a family doctor to see a specialist, with some exceptions.

column6: Die Wartezeit für einen Termin ist lang.
column7: The waiting time for an appointment is long.
column8: Long Wartezeiten for specialists are a constant topic of debate in German public healthcare.

column6: Präventivmedizin spart langfristig Kosten.
column7: Preventive medicine saves costs in the long term.
column8: 'Langfristig' comes from 'lang' (long) and 'Frist' (deadline, term): literally 'long-term'.

column6: Die jährliche Vorsorgeuntersuchung ist wichtig.
column7: The annual preventive check-up is important.
column8: In Germany, the annual 'Vorsorgeuntersuchung' is covered free of charge by mandatory health insurance.

column6: Die Epidemie breitete sich schnell aus.
column7: The epidemic spread quickly.
column8: 'Sich ausbreiten' is separable and reflexive, meaning 'to spread', often used in medical contexts.

column6: Die Pandemie veränderte den Alltag vieler Menschen.
column7: The pandemic changed the everyday life of many people.
column8: 'Verändern' takes a direct accusative object, a verb common in discourse about recent major historical events.

column6: Ein starkes Immunsystem schützt vor Krankheiten.
column7: A strong immune system protects against illness.
column8: 'Schützen vor' takes the dative: 'vor Krankheiten' — a common fixed structure in medical contexts.

column6: Er leidet an einer chronischen Krankheit.
column7: He suffers from a chronic illness.
column8: 'Leiden an' takes the dative: 'an einer Krankheit' — a common fixed structure for describing persistent medical conditions.

column6: Der Arzt konnte keine klare Diagnose stellen.
column7: The doctor couldn't make a clear diagnosis.
column8: 'Eine Diagnose stellen' is the standard fixed collocation used in all formal medical contexts.

column6: Dieses Medikament hat starke Nebenwirkungen.
column7: This medication has strong side effects.
column8: 'Nebenwirkung' combines 'Neben-' (alongside, secondary) and 'Wirkung' (effect): a drug's secondary effect.

column6: Es gibt Wechselwirkungen zwischen den Medikamenten.
column7: There are interactions between the medications.
column8: 'Zwischen' takes the dative when indicating a static position or relationship between two or more things.

column6: Der Klinikaufenthalt dauerte drei Tage.
column7: The hospital stay lasted three days.
column8: 'Klinikaufenthalt' combines 'Klinik' and 'Aufenthalt' (stay): a formal term for a hospital admission.

column6: Nachhaltige Stadtentwicklung ist ein zentrales Thema.
column7: Sustainable urban development is a central topic.
column8: 'Stadtentwicklung' combines 'Stadt' (city) and 'Entwicklung' (development), a key term in urban planning.

column6: Die Verkehrswende soll Autos reduzieren.
column7: The transport transition is meant to reduce cars.
column8: 'Verkehrswende' echoes the better-known 'Energiewende' (energy transition), applying the same concept to transport.

column6: Die Innenstadt hat eine große Fußgängerzone.
column7: The city center has a large pedestrian zone.
column8: Pedestrian zones have been common in German old towns since the 1970s, among the first in Europe.

column6: Der neue Radweg ist sehr sicher.
column7: The new cycle path is very safe.
column8: Cities like Münster and Karlsruhe are famous in Germany for their extensive network of Radwege.

column6: Der öffentliche Nahverkehr ist hier gut ausgebaut.
column7: Public local transport here is well developed.
column8: 'Ausgebaut' comes from 'ausbauen' (to expand, develop), often referring to public infrastructure.

column6: Mit dem Deutschlandticket fahre ich günstig durch das ganze Land.
column7: With the Deutschlandticket I travel cheaply across the whole country.
column8: Introduced in 2023, the Deutschlandticket offers unlimited local public transport nationwide for a fixed monthly price.

column6: Die Verkehrsplanung berücksichtigt auch Fußgänger.
column7: Transport planning also takes pedestrians into account.
column8: 'Berücksichtigen' takes a direct accusative object, a formal verb used in administrative and technical contexts.

column6: Der Stadtplaner entwirft neue Wohnviertel.
column7: The urban planner designs new residential districts.
column8: 'Entwerfen' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to design', a verb with the always-inseparable prefix 'ent-'.

column6: Die Stadt braucht mehr Grünflächen.
column7: The city needs more green spaces.
column8: 'Grünfläche' combines 'grün' (green) and 'Fläche' (area): a technical term for parks and public gardens.

column6: Verdichtung bedeutet mehr Wohnraum auf weniger Fläche.
column7: Densification means more living space on less area.
column8: 'Verdichtung' comes from 'verdichten' (to condense, thicken), a technical term in urban planning.

column6: Die Stadt will neuen Wohnraum schaffen.
column7: The city wants to create new housing.
column8: 'Schaffen' is a strong irregular verb: 'schuf, geschaffen', different from the regular 'schaffen' (to manage to do).

column6: Der Bauboom hat die Preise erhöht.
column7: The construction boom has driven up prices.
column8: 'Erhöhen' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to raise', often used for prices or rates.

column6: Trotz Wohnungsnot gibt es Leerstand.
column7: Despite the housing shortage, there's vacancy.
column8: 'Leerstand' combines 'leer' (empty) and 'Stand' (state): a property left empty, often for speculative reasons.

column6: Die Wohnungsnot betrifft besonders junge Familien.
column7: The housing shortage especially affects young families.
column8: 'Besonders' reinforces the statement by pointing to a group particularly affected by a phenomenon.

column6: Die neue U-Bahn-Station ist barrierefrei.
column7: The new subway station is accessible.
column8: 'Barrierefrei' combines 'Barriere' (barrier) and 'frei' (free): the absence of obstacles for people with disabilities.

column6: Für Rollstuhlfahrer gibt es einen separaten Eingang.
column7: There's a separate entrance for wheelchair users.
column8: 'Rollstuhlfahrer' combines 'Rollstuhl' (wheelchair) and 'Fahrer' (one who drives/uses a vehicle).

column6: Menschen mit Beeinträchtigung brauchen mehr Unterstützung.
column7: People with impairments need more support.
column8: 'Beeinträchtigung' means a limitation or damage; 'Menschen mit Beeinträchtigung' is now a common phrase for people with disabilities.

column6: Unternehmen müssen Verantwortung für ihre Produkte übernehmen.
column7: Companies must take responsibility for their products.
column8: 'Übernehmen für' takes the accusative: 'für ihre Produkte' — a fixed structure in ethical and corporate contexts.

column6: Die Wettbewerbsfähigkeit der Firma steigt.
column7: The company's competitiveness is rising.
column8: A very long compound typical of economic language: 'Wettbewerb' (competition) + 'Fähigkeit' (capability).

column6: Die Innovationskraft deutscher Firmen ist bekannt.
column7: The innovative power of German companies is well known.
column8: Germany is traditionally associated with a strong 'Mittelstand', innovative and often specialized small and medium enterprises.

column6: Die Firma entwickelt eine neue Digitalstrategie.
column7: The company is developing a new digital strategy.
column8: 'Entwickeln' takes a direct accusative object, a verb common in corporate and technology language.

column6: Der Automatisierungsgrad ist in dieser Branche hoch.
column7: The degree of automation in this sector is high.
column8: A long compound: 'Automatisierung' + 'Grad' (degree), typical of industrial and statistical language.

column6: Die Wertschöpfung findet zunehmend digital statt.
column7: Value creation increasingly takes place digitally.
column8: 'Stattfinden' is separable: 'findet statt' in the present tense, used to describe where/how a process happens.

column6: Skalierbarkeit ist für Start-ups entscheidend.
column7: Scalability is decisive for startups.
column8: 'Skalierbarkeit' comes from 'skalieren' (to scale), a technical loan from Anglo-Saxon economic language.

column6: Ihr Geschäftsmodell ist sehr innovativ.
column7: Their business model is very innovative.
column8: 'Geschäftsmodell' combines 'Geschäft' (business) and 'Modell' (model), a standard term in the entrepreneurial world.

column6: Wer ist die Zielgruppe dieser Kampagne?
column7: Who is the target audience of this campaign?
column8: 'Zielgruppe' combines 'Ziel' (target/goal) and 'Gruppe' (group): the group a campaign is aimed at.

column6: Die Markenidentität muss konsistent sein.
column7: Brand identity must be consistent.
column8: 'Markenidentität' combines 'Marke' (brand) and 'Identität' (identity), a key term in marketing.

column6: Kundenbindung ist wichtiger als Neukundengewinnung.
column7: Customer loyalty is more important than acquiring new customers.
column8: 'Wichtiger als' takes the comparative with 'als' to introduce the second term of comparison.

column6: Kundenzufriedenheit wird regelmäßig gemessen.
column7: Customer satisfaction is measured regularly.
column8: 'Gemessen werden' is passive, used to describe systematic corporate evaluation processes.

column6: Der Onlinehandel wächst jedes Jahr.
column7: E-commerce grows every year.
column8: 'Onlinehandel' combines the English loanword 'Online' with the German word 'Handel' (trade).

column6: Die Lieferkette wurde durch die Krise gestört.
column7: The supply chain was disrupted by the crisis.
column8: 'Wurde gestört' is passive in the Präteritum: 'werden' plus a participle, common in economic journalism.

column6: Deutschland importiert viele Rohstoffe.
column7: Germany imports a lot of raw materials.
column8: Despite being an industrial power, Germany depends heavily on imported raw materials.

column6: Das Handelsabkommen wird neu verhandelt.
column7: The trade agreement is being renegotiated.
column8: 'Neu verhandeln' means 'to renegotiate from scratch', a fixed structure in diplomatic and economic language.

column6: Auf importierte Waren fallen Zollgebühren an.
column7: Customs duties apply to imported goods.
column8: 'Anfallen' is separable and means 'to accrue, apply', often used for costs or fees.

column6: Deutschland hat traditionell einen Exportüberschuss.
column7: Germany has traditionally had a trade surplus.
column8: Germany is known for its strong trade surplus, often a subject of debate in the European economy.

column6: Die Wirtschaft steuert auf eine Rezession zu.
column7: The economy is heading toward a recession.
column8: 'Zusteuern auf' is separable and takes the accusative: 'auf eine Rezession zusteuern' — a fixed structure in economic journalism.

column6: Die Konjunktur erholt sich langsam.
column7: The economy is slowly recovering.
column8: 'Sich erholen' is reflexive and means 'to recover', used both economically and physically.

column6: Die Zentralbank erhöht die Zinsen.
column7: The central bank is raising interest rates.
column8: Germany's Bundesbank has historically had a deep influence on the European Central Bank's monetary policy.

column6: Der Leitzins beeinflusst die gesamte Wirtschaft.
column7: The key interest rate affects the entire economy.
column8: 'Beeinflussen' isn't separable: it belongs to the group of verbs with the always-inseparable prefix 'be-'.

column6: Die Kaufkraft der Löhne sinkt.
column7: The purchasing power of wages is falling.
column8: 'Kaufkraft' combines 'kaufen' (to buy) and 'Kraft' (power): the buying capacity of money earned.

column6: Der Mindestlohn wurde erneut erhöht.
column7: The minimum wage was raised again.
column8: Germany's legal minimum wage was only introduced in 2015, relatively late compared to other European countries.

column6: Die Tarifverhandlungen sind gescheitert.
column7: The collective bargaining talks have failed.
column8: 'Gescheitert' comes from 'scheitern' (to fail), conjugated with 'sein' in the Perfekt like all verbs of change of state.

column6: Der Sozialstaat schützt die Schwächsten.
column7: The welfare state protects the weakest.
column8: The German Sozialstaat model, developed starting with Bismarck, is among the oldest and most structured in Europe.

column6: Umverteilung ist ein umstrittenes Thema.
column7: Redistribution is a controversial topic.
column8: 'Umstritten' is the past participle of 'umstreiten', used as an adjective to describe something debated.

column6: Deutschland hat eine progressive Besteuerung.
column7: Germany has progressive taxation.
column8: In the German system, the tax rate gradually rises with income, up to a maximum of 45 percent.

column6: Ein bedingungsloses Grundeinkommen wird diskutiert.
column7: An unconditional basic income is being discussed.
column8: 'Bedingungslos' means 'unconditional', used to describe universal basic income proposals.

column6: Gesellschaftlicher Wandel geschieht oft langsam.
column7: Social change often happens slowly.
column8: 'Geschehen' is a strong irregular verb: 'geschah, geschehen', used for events that 'happen' spontaneously.

column6: Manche sprechen von einem Werteverfall.
column7: Some speak of a decline in values.
column8: 'Sprechen von' takes the dative: 'von einem Werteverfall' — a common fixed structure for introducing a topic of discussion.

column6: Individualismus prägt viele westliche Gesellschaften.
column7: Individualism shapes many Western societies.
column8: 'Prägen' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to shape, deeply characterize'.

column6: In manchen Kulturen dominiert der Kollektivismus.
column7: In some cultures, collectivism dominates.
column8: 'Dominieren' takes a direct accusative object or works intransitively, as in this example.

column6: Der Wertewandel zeigt sich besonders bei jungen Menschen.
column7: The shift in values shows especially among young people.
column8: 'Sich zeigen bei' takes the dative: 'bei jungen Menschen' — a common structure for where a phenomenon shows up.

column6: Für viele ist Selbstverwirklichung wichtiger als Sicherheit.
column7: For many, self-actualisation is more important than security.
column8: 'Selbstverwirklichung' combines 'selbst' (self) and 'verwirklichen' (to realize), a key psychological concept.

column6: Ihr Kommunikationsstil ist sehr direkt.
column7: Her communication style is very direct.
column8: German is often perceived as a language of direct communication compared to more indirect styles in other cultures.

column6: Man muss manchmal zwischen den Zeilen lesen.
column7: Sometimes you have to read between the lines.
column8: 'Zwischen den Zeilen' matches the English idiom exactly, referring to a text's implicit meaning.

column6: Körpersprache verrät oft mehr als Worte.
column7: Body language often reveals more than words.
column8: 'Verraten' isn't separable and means 'to betray, reveal', often used figuratively.

column6: Es ist wichtig, Empathie zu zeigen.
column7: It's important to show empathy.
column8: 'Zeigen' takes a direct accusative object and is used for a wide range of qualities and emotions.

column6: Aktives Zuhören verbessert jede Beziehung.
column7: Active listening improves every relationship.
column8: 'Zuhören' as a nominalized infinitive always takes the neuter article 'das', like all nominalized infinitives.

column6: Konfliktlösung erfordert Geduld.
column7: Conflict resolution requires patience.
column8: 'Erfordern' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to require', a formal inseparable verb.

column6: Chefs sollten regelmäßig Feedback geben.
column7: Bosses should give feedback regularly.
column8: 'Feedback geben' is a very common hybrid loan in modern German corporate language.

column6: Kritikfähigkeit ist eine wichtige Kompetenz.
column7: The ability to accept criticism is an important skill.
column8: 'Kritikfähigkeit' combines 'Kritik' and 'Fähigkeit' (ability): the ability to receive criticism constructively.

column6: Selbstwahrnehmung und Fremdwahrnehmung unterscheiden sich oft.
column7: Self-perception and others' perception often differ.
column8: 'Sich unterscheiden' is reflexive and means 'to differ', used to compare two things.

column6: Introvertiertheit wird oft missverstanden.
column7: Introversion is often misunderstood.
column8: 'Missverstanden werden' is passive, used to describe a mistaken social perception.

column6: Extrovertiertheit hilft beim Netzwerken.
column7: Extroversion helps with networking.
column8: 'Beim Netzwerken' uses the dative after 'bei', a common preposition indicating the context of an action.

column6: Übermäßiges Grübeln schadet der Psyche.
column7: Excessive brooding harms the psyche.
column8: 'Schaden' takes the dative: 'der Psyche', one of the most common dative verbs in German.

column6: Verdrängung ist ein psychologischer Abwehrmechanismus.
column7: Repression is a psychological defense mechanism.
column8: The concept of 'Verdrängung' was formulated in German by Sigmund Freud, the founder of psychoanalysis.

column6: Träume spiegeln oft das Unterbewusstsein wider.
column7: Dreams often reflect the subconscious.
column8: 'Widerspiegeln' is separable: 'spiegeln wider' in the present tense, meaning 'to reflect' figuratively.

column6: Es braucht Zeit, ein Trauma zu verarbeiten.
column7: It takes time to process a trauma.
column8: 'Verarbeiten' isn't separable and means 'to process', used for both trauma and information in general.

column6: Emotionale Intelligenz lässt sich trainieren.
column7: Emotional intelligence can be trained.
column8: 'Sich trainieren lassen' expresses passive possibility: 'lets itself be trained', i.e. 'can be trained'.

column6: Achtsamkeitstraining reduziert nachweislich Stress.
column7: Mindfulness training demonstrably reduces stress.
column8: 'Nachweislich' comes from 'nachweisen' (to prove), a formal adverb typical of scientific language.

column6: Dieser Wald ist ein Naturschutzgebiet.
column7: This forest is a nature reserve.
column8: Germany has thousands of Naturschutzgebiete, many established as far back as the 1930s.

column6: Der Wald ist ein empfindliches Ökosystem.
column7: The forest is a sensitive ecosystem.
column8: 'Empfindlich' means 'sensitive, delicate', often used environmentally to describe ecological fragility.

column6: Biodiversität ist entscheidend für stabile Ökosysteme.
column7: Biodiversity is crucial for stable ecosystems.
column8: 'Biodiversität' and 'Artenvielfalt' are near-synonyms, the first more technical-scientific, the second more colloquial.

column6: Der Lebensraum vieler Tiere schrumpft.
column7: The habitat of many animals is shrinking.
column8: 'Schrumpfen' means 'to shrink', a regular verb common in discourse about biodiversity loss.

column6: Wiederaufforstung hilft dem Klima.
column7: Reforestation helps the climate.
column8: 'Helfen' takes the dative: 'dem Klima', one of the most frequent dative verbs along with 'helfen', 'danken', and 'gehören'.

column6: Der CO2-Ausstoß muss drastisch sinken.
column7: CO2 emissions must fall drastically.
column8: 'Drastisch sinken' is a strong collocation, common in political speeches about climate.

column6: Deutschland strebt Klimaneutralität bis 2045 an.
column7: Germany is aiming for climate neutrality by 2045.
column8: 'Anstreben' is separable and takes the accusative: 'strebt an', a formal verb indicating an ambitious goal.

column6: Die CO2-Steuer soll klimaschädliches Verhalten teurer machen.
column7: The carbon tax is meant to make climate-damaging behavior more expensive.
column8: 'Teurer machen' is the standard structure for 'to make more expensive', a common causative in German.

column6: Der europäische Emissionshandel setzt Preise für CO2.
column7: European emissions trading sets prices for CO2.
column8: 'Setzen' takes a direct accusative object with no preposition, a technical verb used in economic-environmental contexts.

column6: Kreislaufwirtschaft reduziert Abfall drastisch.
column7: The circular economy drastically cuts waste.
column8: 'Kreislaufwirtschaft' combines 'Kreislauf' (cycle) and 'Wirtschaft' (economy): a waste-free economic model.

column6: Ressourcenschonung ist ein zentrales Prinzip.
column7: Resource conservation is a central principle.
column8: 'Ressourcenschonung' comes from 'schonen' (to spare, take care of), a compound with 'Ressourcen' (resources).

column6: Konsumverzicht ist für viele schwer vorstellbar.
column7: Cutting consumption is hard for many to imagine.
column8: 'Schwer vorstellbar sein' means 'to be hard to imagine' — a fixed adjectival structure.

column6: Jeder kann seinen ökologischen Fußabdruck reduzieren.
column7: Everyone can reduce their ecological footprint.
column8: 'Fußabdruck' combines 'Fuß' (foot) and 'Abdruck' (imprint): the metaphor of the environmental mark each person leaves.

column6: Die Raumfahrt fasziniert viele Kinder.
column7: Space travel fascinates many children.
column8: 'Raumfahrt' combines 'Raum' (space) and 'Fahrt' (journey): literally 'journey into space'.

column6: Der Weltraum bleibt größtenteils unerforscht.
column7: Outer space remains largely unexplored.
column8: 'Größtenteils' means 'mostly', an adverb made of 'größt-' (biggest) and 'Teil' (part).

column6: Der Satellit sendet wichtige Daten.
column7: The satellite sends important data.
column8: 'Senden' means both 'to send' and 'to broadcast' via radio or TV — a frequent technical double meaning.

column6: Quantenphysik ist schwer zu verstehen.
column7: Quantum physics is hard to understand.
column8: 'Schwer zu verstehen' takes the infinitive with 'zu', the standard structure for expressing difficulty in understanding.

column6: Genforschung wirft ethische Fragen auf.
column7: Genetic research raises ethical questions.
column8: 'Aufwerfen' is separable and means 'to raise (a question)': 'wirft auf' in the present tense.

column6: Gentechnik wird kontrovers diskutiert.
column7: Genetic engineering is discussed controversially.
column8: 'Kontrovers diskutiert werden' is passive, often used to describe publicly debated topics.

column6: Stammzellenforschung eröffnet neue Möglichkeiten.
column7: Stem cell research opens up new possibilities.
column8: 'Eröffnen' isn't separable and takes a direct accusative object, meaning 'to open' figuratively or literally.

column6: Klonen von Tieren ist rechtlich umstritten.
column7: Cloning animals is legally controversial.
column8: 'Von' takes the dative and here indicates the object of the cloning: 'Klonen von Tieren' (cloning of animals).

column6: Das menschliche Erbgut ist fast vollständig entschlüsselt.
column7: The human genome has almost fully been decoded.
column8: 'Entschlüsselt' comes from 'entschlüsseln' (to decode), a verb sharing a root with 'Schlüssel' (key).

column6: Unter dem Mikroskop sieht man Details.
column7: Under the microscope you can see details.
column8: 'Unter dem Mikroskop' uses the dative: a position under the instrument, with no movement implied.

column6: Mit einem starken Teleskop sieht man ferne Galaxien.
column7: With a powerful telescope you can see distant galaxies.
column8: 'Mit' takes the dative, used here to indicate the instrument used for observation.

column6: Der Große Wagen ist ein bekanntes Sternbild.
column7: The Big Dipper is a well-known constellation.
column8: 'Sternbild' combines 'Stern' (star) and 'Bild' (image): the image formed by a group of stars.

column6: Die Sonnenfinsternis war ein seltenes Erlebnis.
column7: The solar eclipse was a rare experience.
column8: 'Sonnenfinsternis' combines 'Sonne' (sun) and 'Finsternis' (darkness): literally 'darkness of the sun'.

column6: Die Evolutionstheorie erklärt die Artenvielfalt.
column7: The theory of evolution explains species diversity.
column8: 'Erklären' takes a direct accusative object with no preposition, a verb common in scientific discourse.

column6: Sie studiert Ökonomie an der Universität.
column7: She studies economics at university.
column8: 'Ökonomie' is more technical-academic than 'Wirtschaft', used specifically for the scientific discipline.

column6: Soziologie untersucht das menschliche Zusammenleben.
column7: Sociology studies human coexistence.
column8: 'Untersuchen' isn't separable and takes a direct accusative object, used to describe systematic study of a phenomenon.

column6: Anthropologie erforscht menschliche Kulturen.
column7: Anthropology researches human cultures.
column8: 'Erforschen' isn't separable and means 'to explore, study in depth', used in academic contexts.

column6: Linguistik beschäftigt sich mit der Struktur von Sprache.
column7: Linguistics deals with the structure of language.
column8: 'Sich beschäftigen mit' takes the dative: 'mit der Struktur' — a very common reflexive structure in academia.

column6: Die Grammatikstruktur des Deutschen ist komplex.
column7: The grammatical structure of German is complex.
column8: A technical compound: 'Grammatik' + 'Struktur', used in linguistic and educational contexts.

column6: Der deutsche Satzbau unterscheidet sich stark vom Italienischen.
column7: German sentence structure differs greatly from Italian.
column8: 'Sich unterscheiden von' takes the dative: 'vom Italienischen' — a fixed structure for linguistic comparisons.

column6: Lesen hilft, den Wortschatz zu erweitern.
column7: Reading helps expand your vocabulary.
column8: 'Erweitern' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to expand', a verb common in educational contexts.

column6: Diese Redewendung kannte ich noch nicht.
column7: I didn't know this idiom yet.
column8: 'Redewendung' combines 'Rede' (speech) and 'Wendung' (turn): a fixed, figurative expression of language.

column6: Dieses Sprichwort gibt es auch auf Italienisch.
column7: This proverb also exists in Italian.
column8: 'Sprichwort' combines 'sprechen' (to speak) and 'Wort' (word): literally 'the word that is said', a traditional saying.

column6: Ich habe es wortwörtlich übersetzt.
column7: I translated it word for word.
column8: 'Wortwörtlich' reinforces 'wörtlich' (literal) by doubling the idea of 'Wort' (word) for maximum emphasis.

column6: Sinngemäß bedeutet das etwa 'ohne Zweifel'.
column7: In essence that means roughly 'without doubt'.
column8: 'Sinngemäß' combines 'Sinn' (meaning) and 'gemäß' (according to): translating by meaning, not literally.

column6: Die Feinheiten der Sprache lernt man erst spät.
column7: You only learn the nuances of a language late on.
column8: 'Feinheiten' comes from 'fein' (fine, subtle), almost always used in the plural for subtle details.

column6: Seine Ausdrucksweise ist sehr elegant.
column7: His manner of expression is very elegant.
column8: 'Ausdrucksweise' combines 'Ausdruck' (expression) and 'Weise' (manner), a formal term in stylistic analysis.

column6: Ironie ist ein häufiges Stilmittel.
column7: Irony is a frequent stylistic device.
column8: 'Stilmittel' combines 'Stil' (style) and 'Mittel' (means): a rhetorical tool used to achieve an effect.

column6: Ironie ist schwer zu übersetzen.
column7: Irony is hard to translate.
column8: 'Schwer zu übersetzen' takes the infinitive with 'zu', used to express difficulty in a specific task.

column6: Sein Sarkasmus kommt nicht bei jedem gut an.
column7: Not everyone appreciates his sarcasm.
column8: 'Ankommen bei' takes the dative: 'bei jedem' — an idiom for 'to go over well with someone'.

column6: Dieses Wortspiel funktioniert nur auf Deutsch.
column7: This pun only works in German.
column8: 'Wortspiel' combines 'Wort' (word) and 'Spiel' (game): a linguistic game based on ambiguity or similar sounds.

column6: Der Roman enthält viele historische Anspielungen.
column7: The novel contains many historical allusions.
column8: 'Enthalten' isn't separable and always takes a direct accusative object, used to describe a text's content.

column6: Das war eine kleine Übertreibung.
column7: That was a slight exaggeration.
column8: 'Übertreibung' comes from 'übertreiben' (to exaggerate), an inseparable verb with the fixed prefix 'über-'.

column6: Die Architektur der Stadt ist beeindruckend.
column7: The city's architecture is impressive.
column8: The Bauhaus, an architectural movement born in Germany in the 1920s, influenced modern design worldwide.

column6: Die Fassade wurde restauriert.
column7: The facade was restored.
column8: 'Wurde restauriert' is passive in the Präteritum, common for describing completed restoration work.

column6: Das Gebäude steht unter Denkmalschutz.
column7: The building is under heritage protection.
column8: 'Unter Denkmalschutz stehen' is the standard fixed phrase for saying a building is legally protected.

column6: Frankfurt hat die meisten Wolkenkratzer Deutschlands.
column7: Frankfurt has the most skyscrapers in Germany.
column8: Frankfurt am Main is nicknamed 'Mainhattan' precisely for its skyline of skyscrapers, unusual for the rest of the country.

column6: Viele Häuser im Norden sind aus Backstein gebaut.
column7: Many houses in the north are built from brick.
column8: Red-brick architecture ('Backsteingotik') is typical of northern Hanseatic cities like Lübeck and Hamburg.

column6: Heute wird der Grundstein für das neue Museum gelegt.
column7: Today the foundation stone for the new museum is being laid.
column8: 'Den Grundstein legen für' is a fixed expression, used both literally and figuratively for a new beginning.

column6: Das alte Haus hat großen Renovierungsbedarf.
column7: The old house is badly in need of renovation.
column8: 'Renovierungsbedarf' combines 'Renovierung' and 'Bedarf' (need), a technical real-estate term.

column6: Die Innenausstattung ist modern und funktional.
column7: The interior fittings are modern and functional.
column8: 'Innenausstattung' combines 'innen' (inside) and 'Ausstattung' (fitting, equipment).

column6: Die Symmetrie des Gebäudes wirkt beruhigend.
column7: The building's symmetry feels calming.
column8: 'Wirken' means 'to appear, have an effect', a common verb for describing the impression something gives.

column6: Die Silhouette der Stadt ist unverwechselbar.
column7: The city's skyline is unmistakable.
column8: 'Silhouette' is a loanword from French, kept almost identical even in German pronunciation.

column6: Meteorologen treffen täglich neue Wettervorhersagen.
column7: Meteorologists make new weather forecasts daily.
column8: 'Eine Vorhersage treffen' is the fixed collocation, an alternative to 'eine Vorhersage machen'.

column6: Deutschland liegt in einer gemäßigten Klimazone.
column7: Germany lies in a temperate climate zone.
column8: 'Gemäßigt' comes from 'mäßigen' (to moderate): a 'moderate' climate, neither too hot nor too cold.

column6: Extremwetter nimmt weltweit zu.
column7: Extreme weather is increasing worldwide.
column8: 'Zunehmen' is separable and means 'to increase', a verb very common in climate-change discourse.

column6: Die Dürre schädigt die Ernte.
column7: The drought is damaging the harvest.
column8: 'Schädigen' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to damage', a formal verb used in agricultural contexts.

column6: Die Überschwemmung zerstörte viele Häuser.
column7: The flood destroyed many houses.
column8: 'Zerstören' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to destroy', a verb common in natural-disaster journalism.

column6: Naturkatastrophen nehmen an Häufigkeit zu.
column7: Natural disasters are increasing in frequency.
column8: 'An Häufigkeit zunehmen' is a fixed structure for expressing an increase in a phenomenon's frequency.

column6: Ein Frühwarnsystem kann Leben retten.
column7: An early warning system can save lives.
column8: 'Retten' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to save', a verb common in public-safety contexts.

column6: Der Katastrophenschutz koordiniert die Rettungskräfte.
column7: Civil protection coordinates the rescue teams.
column8: 'Koordinieren' takes a direct accusative object, a Latin loanword common in institutional language.

column6: Der Meeresspiegel steigt kontinuierlich.
column7: Sea level is rising continuously.
column8: 'Meeresspiegel' combines 'Meer' (sea) and 'Spiegel' (mirror): literally 'the mirror of the sea'.

column6: Die Gletscher in den Alpen schmelzen schnell.
column7: The glaciers in the Alps are melting quickly.
column8: 'Schmelzen' uses 'sein' in the Perfekt when describing a complete change of state: 'ist geschmolzen'.

column6: Das Auftauen des Permafrosts ist besorgniserregend.
column7: The thawing of permafrost is worrying.
column8: 'Permafrost' is ground frozen all year round, mainly in Siberia, Alaska and Canada. It is masculine: 'der Permafrost'.

column6: Küstenschutz wird immer teurer.
column7: Coastal protection is getting more and more expensive.
column8: Dutch and German North Sea dikes are among the most advanced coastal-protection systems in the world.

column6: Der Deich schützt das Land vor Überschwemmungen.
column7: The dike protects the land from flooding.
column8: 'Schützen vor' takes the dative: 'vor Überschwemmungen' — a common fixed structure in discourse about protection.

column6: Die Sturmflut von 1962 war verheerend.
column7: The 1962 storm surge was devastating.
column8: The great Hamburg flood of 1962, caused by a Sturmflut, is among the best-known natural disasters in recent German history.

column6: Verhandlungsgeschick ist in diesem Job entscheidend.
column7: Negotiating skill is decisive in this job.
column8: 'Verhandlungsgeschick' combines 'Verhandlung' (negotiation) and 'Geschick' (skill, dexterity).

column6: Sie hat großes Durchsetzungsvermögen.
column7: She has great assertiveness.
column8: A long compound: 'durchsetzen' (to assert) + 'Vermögen' (capacity), typical of HR language.

column6: Ihr Improvisationstalent hat uns gerettet.
column7: Her talent for improvisation saved us.
column8: 'Talent' often takes 'für' + accusative, but also appears as the first element of a compound, as here.

column6: Entscheidungsfreudigkeit wird von Führungskräften erwartet.
column7: Decisiveness is expected of managers.
column8: 'Erwartet werden von' takes the dative after 'von', a passive structure common in professional-skills language.

column6: Seine Detailversessenheit hat auch Nachteile.
column7: His obsession with detail also has downsides.
column8: 'Versessenheit' comes from 'versessen sein auf' (to be fixated on), a participial adjective turned abstract noun.

column6: Multitasking-Fähigkeit wird oft überschätzt.
column7: Multitasking ability is often overrated.
column8: 'Überschätzt werden' is passive, a common structure for criticizing excessive expectations of a trait.

column6: Der Anpassungsdruck in der Branche ist hoch.
column7: The pressure to adapt in the industry is high.
column8: 'Anpassungsdruck' combines 'Anpassung' (adaptation) and 'Druck' (pressure), typical of economic language.

column6: Zu viel Konkurrenzdenken schadet dem Team.
column7: Too much of a competitive mindset harms the team.
column8: 'Schaden' takes the dative: 'dem Team', one of the most frequent dative verbs in German.

column6: Gemeinsame Projekte fördern die Zusammenarbeit.
column7: Shared projects promote collaboration.
column8: 'Fördern' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to promote', very common in team-building language.

column6: Die Fusion soll Synergieeffekte schaffen.
column7: The merger is meant to create synergy effects.
column8: 'Synergieeffekt' combines the Greek loanword 'Synergie' with 'Effekt', typical of corporate jargon.

column6: Die Unternehmensfusion wurde genehmigt.
column7: The corporate merger was approved.
column8: 'Wurde genehmigt' is passive in the Präteritum, the standard structure for official announcements of corporate decisions.

column6: Der Marktanteil ist stark gesunken.
column7: Market share has fallen sharply.
column8: 'Marktanteil' combines 'Markt' (market) and 'Anteil' (share), a key term in economic analysis.

column6: Die Firma plant eine Expansion nach Asien.
column7: The company is planning an expansion into Asia.
column8: 'Expansion' is the noun of 'expandieren' (to expand); for a company you also say 'Wachstum' (growth).

column6: Die Nähe zum Hafen ist ein Standortvorteil.
column7: Proximity to the port is a locational advantage.
column8: 'Standortvorteil' combines 'Standort' (location) and 'Vorteil' (advantage), a key term in economic geography.

column6: Die neue Vertriebsstrategie zeigt Wirkung.
column7: The new sales strategy is showing results.
column8: 'Wirkung zeigen' is the standard fixed collocation for saying something 'is working, producing results'.

column6: Kundenakquise kostet viel Zeit.
column7: Customer acquisition takes a lot of time.
column8: 'Akquise' is a shortened loanword from the Latin 'Akquisition', widely used in German marketing jargon.

column6: Der Sportler ist Markenbotschafter der Firma.
column7: The athlete is the company's brand ambassador.
column8: 'Markenbotschafter' combines 'Marke' (brand) and 'Botschafter' (ambassador), an influencer-marketing role.

column6: Der Post hat eine große Reichweite erzielt.
column7: The post achieved a large reach.
column8: 'Erzielen' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to achieve', common in digital-marketing language.

column6: Influencer-Marketing wächst rasant.
column7: Influencer marketing is growing rapidly.
column8: 'Rasant' means 'extremely fast, dizzying', a colloquial but widespread adjective in modern economic language.

column6: Die Algorithmus-Änderung betrifft alle Nutzer.
column7: The algorithm change affects all users.
column8: 'Betreffen' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to concern', a formal inseparable verb.

column6: Das Nutzerverhalten verändert sich schnell.
column7: User behavior is changing quickly.
column8: 'Nutzerverhalten' combines 'Nutzer' (user) and 'Verhalten' (behavior), a key term in digital analytics.

column6: Suchmaschinenoptimierung ist für Firmen wichtig.
column7: Search engine optimization is important for companies.
column8: A very long compound, often abbreviated 'SEO' in German too, from the English 'search engine optimization'.

column6: Eine gute Onlinepräsenz ist heute unverzichtbar.
column7: A good online presence is indispensable today.
column8: 'Unverzichtbar' combines the negating 'ver-' and 'zichten' (to renounce): literally 'that cannot be given up'.

column6: Die Erwartungshaltung der Eltern belastet viele Kinder.
column7: Parents' attitude of expectation weighs on many children.
column8: 'Belasten' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to burden', common in psychological discourse.

column6: Leistungsdruck in der Schule nimmt zu.
column7: Performance pressure at school is increasing.
column8: 'Leistungsdruck' combines 'Leistung' (performance) and 'Druck' (pressure), a much-discussed topic in German education.

column6: Perfektionismus kann lähmend wirken.
column7: Perfectionism can have a paralyzing effect.
column8: 'Lähmend wirken' means 'to have a paralyzing effect', used in psychological contexts.

column6: Prokrastination betrifft fast jeden Studenten.
column7: Procrastination affects nearly every student.
column8: 'Prokrastination' is an academic loanword from Latin, increasingly common in colloquial German too.

column6: Meine Aufschieberitis wird immer schlimmer.
column7: My chronic procrastination keeps getting worse.
column8: 'Aufschieberitis' is a jokey word: 'aufschieben' (to postpone) plus the medical suffix '-itis', as if it were a disease.

column6: Gutes Zeitmanagement reduziert Stress.
column7: Good time management reduces stress.
column8: 'Zeitmanagement' combines the English loanword 'Management' with the German word 'Zeit' (time).

column6: Experten raten, Multitasking zu vermeiden.
column7: Experts advise avoiding multitasking.
column8: 'Vermeiden' takes the accusative: 'Stress vermeiden'. It is inseparable and irregular: 'er vermied', 'hat vermieden'.

column6: Es fällt mir schwer, den Fokus zu behalten.
column7: I find it hard to stay focused.
column8: 'Es fällt mir schwer' takes the dative and means 'it's hard for me', a very common German structure.

column6: Ich versuche, Ablenkungen zu vermeiden.
column7: I try to avoid distractions.
column8: 'Ablenkung' comes from 'ablenken' (to distract), a separable verb very common in productivity discourse.

column6: Eine Prioritätenliste hilft bei der Organisation.
column7: A priority list helps with organization.
column8: 'Bei der Organisation' uses the dative after 'bei', indicating the context in which something helps.

column6: Die Aufgabenverteilung im Team ist unklar.
column7: Task distribution in the team is unclear.
column8: 'Aufgabenverteilung' combines 'Aufgabe' (task) and 'Verteilung' (distribution), a common term in project management.

column6: Wir arbeiten unter großem Zeitdruck.
column7: We're working under great time pressure.
column8: 'Unter Zeitdruck' uses the dative: the position 'under' pressure, with no movement implied.

column6: Termindruck führt oft zu Fehlern.
column7: Deadline pressure often leads to mistakes.
column8: 'Führen zu' takes the dative: 'zu Fehlern' — a common fixed structure for describing a negative consequence.

column6: Neue Software soll die Effizienz steigern.
column7: New software is meant to increase efficiency.
column8: 'Steigern' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to increase', common in corporate language.

column6: Produktivität lässt sich nicht immer leicht messen.
column7: Productivity isn't always easy to measure.
column8: 'Sich messen lassen' expresses passive possibility: 'lets itself be measured', i.e. 'can be measured'.

column6: Ein gutes Arbeitsklima motiviert die Mitarbeiter.
column7: A good work atmosphere motivates employees.
column8: 'Arbeitsklima' combines 'Arbeit' (work) and 'Klima' (climate) figuratively, referring to the office atmosphere.

column6: Das Betriebsklima hat sich verschlechtert.
column7: The company atmosphere has worsened.
column8: 'Sich verschlechtern' is reflexive and means 'to worsen', the opposite of 'sich verbessern'.

column6: Die Fluktuation ist in dieser Branche hoch.
column7: Staff turnover is high in this industry.
column8: 'Fluktuation' is nearly identical across languages, a shared economic term of Latin origin.

column6: Mitarbeiterbindung spart langfristig Kosten.
column7: Employee retention saves costs in the long run.
column8: 'Mitarbeiterbindung' combines 'Mitarbeiter' (employee) and 'Bindung' (bond), a key term in HR.

column6: Nachwuchsförderung ist eine Investition in die Zukunft.
column7: Talent development is an investment in the future.
column8: 'Nachwuchsförderung' combines 'Nachwuchs' (up-and-coming talent) and 'Förderung' (promotion), common in corporate and sports language.

column6: Diversität bereichert Teams nachweislich.
column7: Diversity demonstrably enriches teams.
column8: 'Diversität' is the preferred term in corporate language over the more generic 'Vielfalt'.

column6: Die Firma entwickelt eine neue Inklusionsstrategie.
column7: The company is developing a new inclusion strategy.
column8: 'Entwickeln' takes a direct accusative object, a verb common in corporate planning language.

column6: Gehaltstransparenz wird zunehmend gefordert.
column7: Salary transparency is increasingly being demanded.
column8: 'Gefordert werden' is passive, common in discourse about workers' rights.

column6: Das Lohngefälle zwischen den Geschlechtern besteht weiterhin.
column7: The pay gap between the genders still persists.
column8: 'Zwischen' takes the dative, used to indicate a relationship between two groups.

column6: Diese Stelle bietet gute Karrierechancen.
column7: This position offers good career opportunities.
column8: 'Bieten' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to offer', a verb common in job postings.

column6: Es gibt kaum Aufstiegsmöglichkeiten in dieser Firma.
column7: There are hardly any promotion opportunities at this company.
column8: 'Aufstiegsmöglichkeit' combines 'Aufstieg' (rise, advancement) and 'Möglichkeit' (possibility).

column6: Quereinsteiger bringen frische Perspektiven.
column7: Career changers bring fresh perspectives.
column8: 'Quereinsteiger' combines 'quer' (sideways, oblique) and 'einsteigen' (to get on/in): someone entering a field from an unusual angle.

column6: Praktika helfen, Berufserfahrung zu sammeln.
column7: Internships help you gain work experience.
column8: 'Sammeln' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to gather, accumulate', very common with 'Erfahrung' (experience).

column6: Netzwerken ist in vielen Berufen unerlässlich.
column7: Networking is essential in many professions.
column8: 'Unerlässlich' means 'essential', literally 'that cannot be dispensed with without trouble'.

column6: Employer Branding hilft, Talente zu gewinnen.
column7: Employer branding helps attract talent.
column8: A complete English loan phrase, used unchanged in modern German HR jargon.

column6: Ein gutes Onboarding erleichtert den Start.
column7: Good onboarding makes for an easier start.
column8: 'Erleichtern' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to facilitate', a formal inseparable verb.

column6: Die Probezeit dauert sechs Monate.
column7: The probationary period lasts six months.
column8: In Germany, the standard Probezeit is often six months, during which dismissal is easier for both sides.

column6: Beide Seiten müssen die Kündigungsfristen einhalten.
column7: Both sides must observe the notice periods.
column8: 'Einhalten' is separable and takes the accusative, meaning 'to observe, abide by' a deadline or rule.

column6: Der Arbeitgeber muss ein Zeugnis ausstellen.
column7: The employer must issue a reference.
column8: In Germany, every former employee is legally entitled to a formal 'Arbeitszeugnis' at the end of employment.

column6: Nach fünf Jahren hat er endlich eine Beförderung bekommen.
column7: After five years he finally got a promotion.
column8: 'Beförderung' is a career promotion; the verb 'befördern' also means 'to transport': 'Die Bahn befördert Passagiere'.

column6: Für diese Stelle brauchen Sie eine besondere Qualifikation.
column7: You need a special qualification for this position.
column8: 'Qualifikation' means the skills or credentials required for a job; you say 'eine Qualifikation erwerben' (to acquire a qualification).

column6: Sie hat einen befristeten Arbeitsvertrag.
column7: She has a fixed-term employment contract.
column8: 'Befristet' comes from 'Frist' (deadline, term): a contract with a set end date, opposite of 'unbefristet' (permanent).

column6: Innovationsfähigkeit entscheidet über den Erfolg.
column7: Capacity for innovation decides success.
column8: 'Entscheiden über' takes the accusative: 'über den Erfolg' — a fixed structure for expressing what determines an outcome.

column6: Unternehmer brauchen eine gewisse Risikobereitschaft.
column7: Entrepreneurs need a certain willingness to take risks.
column8: 'Risikobereitschaft' combines 'Risiko' (risk) and 'Bereitschaft' (readiness), a key term in entrepreneurial language.

column6: Berlin hat einen lebendigen Gründergeist.
column7: Berlin has a lively entrepreneurial spirit.
column8: 'Gründergeist' combines 'Gründer' (founder) and 'Geist' (spirit), referring to startup culture.

column6: Das Start-up schließt eine neue Finanzierungsrunde ab.
column7: The startup is closing a new funding round.
