column8: 'Abschließen' is separable and takes the accusative: 'schließt ab', used for the formal closing of a deal.

column6: Die Investorensuche gestaltet sich schwierig.
column7: The search for investors is proving difficult.
column8: 'Sich gestalten' is reflexive and means 'to turn out, take shape', a formal verb common in economic language.

column6: Sie haben eine echte Marktlücke gefunden.
column7: They found a real market gap.
column8: 'Marktlücke' combines 'Markt' (market) and 'Lücke' (gap): an unoccupied space in the market.

column6: Die Frist läuft morgen ab.
column7: The deadline expires tomorrow.
column8: 'Frist' is the period or deadline within which something must be done: 'eine Frist einhalten' (to meet it), 'die Frist verlängern'. It is not 'Termin' (appointment).

column6: Er bleibt immer ganz gelassen.
column7: He always stays very calm.
column8: 'Gelassen' is the participle of 'lassen' used as an adjective; the noun is 'Gelassenheit'. It means inner calm, stronger than 'ruhig'.

column6: Er spricht mit großer Bescheidenheit über seinen Erfolg.
column7: He talks about his success with great modesty.
column8: 'Bescheidenheit' comes from 'bescheiden' (modest) with the abstract suffix '-heit'.

column6: Achtsamkeit hilft gegen Stress.
column7: Mindfulness helps against stress.
column8: 'Achtsamkeit' comes from 'achtsam' (attentive, caring), a concept increasingly widespread in modern German wellness culture.

column6: Anpassungsfähigkeit ist im Ausland wichtig.
column7: Adaptability is important abroad.
column8: 'Anpassungsfähigkeit' comes from 'sich anpassen' (to adapt) with the capability suffix '-fähigkeit'.

column6: Mit etwas Willenskraft schaffst du das.
column7: With a bit of willpower, you'll manage it.
column8: 'Willenskraft' combines 'Wille' (will) and 'Kraft' (strength): a very transparent compound.

column6: Ein Studium erfordert Durchhaltevermögen.
column7: A degree requires staying power.
column8: 'Durchhaltevermögen' combines 'durchhalten' (to persevere) and 'Vermögen' (capacity): a very long but transparent compound.

column6: Das Gefühl der Zugehörigkeit ist wichtig.
column7: The feeling of belonging is important.
column8: 'Zugehörigkeit' comes from 'zugehören' (to belong to), an abstract compound with the suffix '-keit'.

column6: Diese Entscheidung war ein Wendepunkt in meinem Leben.
column7: This decision was a turning point in my life.
column8: 'Wendepunkt' combines 'Wende' (turn) and 'Punkt' (point): a decisive moment that changes the course of events.

column6: Eine Versicherung dient der Absicherung.
column7: Insurance serves as a safeguard.
column8: 'Absicherung' comes from 'absichern' (to secure): protection against a risk, for example financial or legal.

column6: Diese Klausel ist im Vertrag wichtig.
column7: This clause is important in the contract.
column8: 'Klausel' is a legal term taken from the Latin 'clausula', nearly identical across many European languages.

column6: Seelische Gesundheit ist genauso wichtig.
column7: Mental health is just as important.
column8: 'Seelisch' comes from 'Seele' (soul), used in contrast with 'körperlich' (physical, bodily).

column6: Der Klimawandel hat globale Auswirkungen.
column7: Climate change has global effects.
column8: 'Auswirkung auf' takes the accusative: 'auf die Umwelt' (on the environment) — a common fixed structure in environmental discourse.

column6: Gleichberechtigung ist im Grundgesetz verankert.
column7: Equal rights are anchored in the constitution.
column8: 'Gleichberechtigung' = 'gleich' (equal) + 'Berechtigung' (entitlement): equal rights for all, often between women and men.

column6: Er bat um Gnade.
column7: He begged for mercy.
column8: Means both 'mercy' and religious 'grace'. Useful expressions: 'Gnade vor Recht ergehen lassen' (to show leniency), 'Gnadenfrist' (period of grace).

column6: Die Idee ist gut, allerdings fehlt das Budget.
column7: The idea is good, though the budget is missing.
column8: 'Allerdings' introduces a restriction or objection, very common in both formal and informal argumentative speech.

column5: to accept / to put up with
column6: Viele nehmen lange Wartezeiten in Kauf.
column7: Many people accept long waiting times.
column8: A fixed phrase: you accept a disadvantage to gain something. 'Kauf' is not literally a purchase here; 'nehmen' is irregular ('er nimmt').

column5: to consider / to take into account
column6: Wir ziehen mehrere Lösungen in Betracht.
column7: We are considering several solutions.
column8: Formal register. A common related phrase is 'in Betracht kommen' (to be an option). 'Ziehen' is irregular: 'hat gezogen'.

column6: Ich vertrage keine Milch, sie liegt mir schwer im Magen.
column7: I can't tolerate milk; it sits heavily in my stomach.
column8: With food, 'vertragen' means your body copes with it; it is irregular (er verträgt). Do not confuse it with 'sich vertragen' (to get along).

column6: Als Beilage gibt es Kartoffeln oder Reis.
column7: The side dish is potatoes or rice.
column8: On menus the main dish and the 'Beilage' are often listed separately; the plural is 'Beilagen'.

column6: Die Soße zum Braten war besonders würzig.
column7: The sauce for the roast was especially flavorful.
column8: Also spelled 'Sauce' (more French-looking); 'Soße' is the usual German form and also means gravy.

column6: Über Geschmack lässt sich bekanntlich nicht streiten.
column7: As is well known, there's no arguing about taste.
column8: 'Geschmack' means both flavor and personal taste; for product flavors use 'Geschmacksrichtungen'.

column6: Die Lebensmittel sind im Supermarkt gerade im Angebot.
column7: Groceries are on special at the supermarket right now.
column8: Usually plural for the weekly shop ('Lebensmittel einkaufen'); 'Essen' is the meal, 'Lebensmittel' the raw foodstuffs.

column6: Wir haben genug Vorrat an Nudeln und Konserven.
column7: We have plenty of pasta and canned food in stock.
column8: Common in 'auf Vorrat kaufen' (to stock up) and 'Vorratsschrank' (pantry); the plural is 'Vorräte'.

column6: Eine warme Mahlzeit am Tag ist mir wichtig.
column7: One hot meal a day is important to me.
column8: 'Mahlzeit!' is also an informal greeting around lunchtime, especially at work; as a noun it simply means 'meal'.

column6: Die Zubereitung des Gerichts dauert nur zwanzig Minuten.
column7: Preparing the dish takes only twenty minutes.
column8: It appears in recipes as the heading for the method; the related verb is 'zubereiten'.

column5: to season to taste, to taste-test
column6: Zum Schluss schmecke ich die Suppe mit Salz ab.
column7: At the end I season the soup to taste with salt.
column8: Separable verb: 'ich schmecke ab'. It means tasting in order to correct the seasoning, not just tasting.

column6: Wir haben heute Abend beim Lieferdienst Pizza bestellt.
column7: Tonight we ordered pizza from the delivery service.
column8: It covers food-delivery apps as well as a shop's own delivery; 'beim Lieferdienst bestellen' is the typical phrase.

column6: Als Nachspeise nehmen wir ein Stück Apfelkuchen.
column7: For dessert we'll have a piece of apple cake.
column8: 'Nachtisch' and 'Dessert' are also used; 'Nachspeise' is especially common in Austria and the south.

column6: Mein Bruder ist seit Jahren Vegetarier.
column7: My brother has been a vegetarian for years.
column8: Feminine 'Vegetarierin'; the adjective is 'vegetarisch'. The plural 'die Vegetarier' is identical to the singular.

column6: Bei Schäden müssen Sie die Hausverwaltung anrufen.
column7: In case of damage you must call the property management.
column8: It manages the building for the owner; it is not the 'Hausmeister', who does the small day-to-day jobs.

column6: Vor der Unterschrift habe ich den Mietvertrag genau gelesen.
column7: Before signing I read the rental agreement carefully.
column8: Plural 'Mietverträge'; 'befristet' or 'unbefristet' gives the term. 'Miete' is the rent money, 'Mietvertrag' the document.

column6: Sie wohnt zur Untermiete in einer kleinen Wohnung.
column7: She lives as a subtenant in a small apartment.
column8: Typical phrase: 'zur Untermiete wohnen'. The person is an 'Untermieter', and the landlord's permission is usually required.

column6: Den Staubsauger stelle ich im Abstellraum ab.
column7: I put the vacuum cleaner away in the storage room.
column8: Plural 'Abstellräume'; for a closet in the flat or cellar. A more colloquial synonym is 'Abstellkammer'.

column6: Die Heizkosten sind im Winter stark gestiegen.
column7: Heating costs rose sharply in winter.
column8: Almost always plural. They are part of the 'Nebenkosten' and paid in advance, with an annual settlement.

column6: Die Warmmiete beträgt neunhundert Euro im Monat.
column7: The rent including utilities is nine hundred euros a month.
column8: Listings distinguish it from 'Kaltmiete' (rent only): 'Warmmiete' includes heating and building charges.

column6: Ein Umtausch ist nur mit Kassenbon möglich.
column7: An exchange is only possible with the receipt.
column8: Often seen on shop signs ('vom Umtausch ausgeschlossen'). Exchanging a faultless item is a courtesy in Germany, not a legal right.

column6: Die Rückgabe der Ware ist innerhalb von vierzehn Tagen möglich.
column7: Returning the goods is possible within fourteen days.
column8: For online purchases there is a 14-day 'Widerrufsrecht'; 'Rückgabe' also applies to deposits and borrowed items.

column6: Vor dem Kauf mache ich immer einen Preisvergleich im Internet.
column7: Before buying, I always compare prices online.
column8: Fixed phrase: 'einen Preisvergleich machen'. Dedicated sites are called 'Preisvergleichsportale'.

column6: Die Retoure wurde gestern vom Paketdienst abgeholt.
column7: The return was picked up by the courier yesterday.
column8: A loanword from French typical of e-commerce: the parcel sent back to the shop. More formal: 'Rücksendung'.

column6: Bitte heben Sie den Kassenbon für den Umtausch auf.
column7: Please keep the receipt for the exchange.
column8: Also called 'Kassenzettel' or 'Bon'. It is not the 'Rechnung' (invoice): it is the till receipt.

column6: Zum Geburtstag habe ich einen Gutschein für die Buchhandlung bekommen.
column7: For my birthday I got a voucher for the bookshop.
column8: Compounds like 'Geschenkgutschein' are common; you redeem it with the verb 'einlösen'.

column6: Im Supermarkt gibt es diese Woche Kaffee im Sonderangebot.
column7: This week the supermarket has coffee on special offer.
column8: Often used as 'im Sonderangebot' or simply 'Angebot'; 'Aktion' is the more commercial leaflet term.

column6: Bargeld ist dort das einzige akzeptierte Zahlungsmittel.
column7: Cash is the only accepted means of payment there.
column8: The plural is identical to the singular. It covers cash, cards and apps; 'gesetzliches Zahlungsmittel' is legal tender.

column6: Bei großen Anschaffungen ist Ratenzahlung oft möglich.
column7: For big purchases, paying in installments is often possible.
column8: You say 'auf Raten kaufen' or 'in Raten zahlen'. Watch the interest rate: 'Zinsen' are often high.

column6: Die Lieferzeit beträgt laut Shop drei bis fünf Werktage.
column7: According to the shop, delivery takes three to five working days.
column8: Found on online product pages; 'Werktage' excludes Sundays and holidays, and Saturdays depend on the shop.

column5: to complain about a defect, to make a claim
column6: Ich möchte den defekten Toaster reklamieren.
column7: I would like to make a claim about the defective toaster.
column8: You claim about a faulty item (accusative): 'etwas reklamieren'. For a general complaint use 'sich beschweren'.

column6: Der Händler hat mir den Kaufpreis sofort erstattet.
column7: The retailer refunded the purchase price to me immediately.
column8: You refund something to someone: 'jemandem etwas erstatten'. The noun is 'Erstattung'; 'zurückzahlen' is more colloquial.

column6: Die Mitgliedschaft im Sportverein kostet zehn Euro im Monat.
column7: Membership in the sports club costs ten euros a month.
column8: You can 'kündigen' (cancel) it with notice; 'Mitglied' is the person, 'Mitgliedschaft' the status.

column6: Am Wochenende fahren wir mit den Kindern in den Freizeitpark.
column7: On the weekend we are going to the amusement park with the kids.
column8: Plural 'Freizeitparks'. It is the neutral term for parks like Europa-Park; 'Vergnügungspark' sounds a little dated.

column6: Der Wanderweg führt durch einen ruhigen Wald zum See.
column7: The hiking trail leads through a quiet forest to the lake.
column8: Plural 'Wanderwege'; trails are marked with colors or symbols. Not to be confused with 'Spazierweg' (an easy stroll path).

column6: Die Veranstaltung findet bei jedem Wetter im Park statt.
column7: The event takes place in the park whatever the weather.
column8: Typical phrase: 'eine Veranstaltung findet statt'. The verb is 'veranstalten', the organizer 'Veranstalter'.

column6: Der Eintritt für Kinder unter sechs Jahren ist frei.
column7: Admission is free for children under six.
column8: 'Eintritt frei' is the sign formula; 'Eintrittskarte' is the ticket, while 'Fahrkarte' is for transport.

column6: Ich habe mich für einen Kurs an der Volkshochschule angemeldet.
column7: I signed up for a course at the adult education center.
column8: The 'Volkshochschule' is the go-to place for evening courses; you 'einen Kurs belegen' or 'besuchen'. 'Kurs' also means exchange rate and heading.

column6: Seine Sammlung alter Münzen ist über hundert Jahre alt.
column7: His collection of old coins is over a hundred years old.
column8: Plural 'Sammlungen'; the verb is 'sammeln' and a collector is a 'Sammler'. It also covers fundraising collections.

column6: Am Sonntagabend spielen wir gern ein Brettspiel.
column7: On Sunday evenings we like to play a board game.
column8: Plural 'Brettspiele'. They are very popular in Germany; 'Gesellschaftsspiel' is the general term for party and family games.
